blocks.text: Streets, schools and getting around Boulevard

items.t: The spine is Grand Boulevard itself: Grand Boulevard and Grand Boulevard Park between Keith Road in the south and Highway 1 in the north (City side), continuing as Grand Boulevard East to Boulevard Crescent and Lynn Valley Road (District side).

Where the condo stock concentrates: nowhere on the corridor — there is none. The corridor's identity is its wide, park-like boulevard frontage with detached houses facing it, under City rules on the City side and District rules on the District side. Listing coverage of the area describes Grand Boulevard as primarily detached homes with larger lots, in contrast to Central Lonsdale's condos and townhomes, and the Boulevard (City) profile states the area is made up mostly of single-family homes.

Heritage frame: Grand Boulevard is a City heritage character area and forms part of the rectilinear system of boulevards and parks known as North Vancouver's Green Necklace, which also includes Victoria Park, Ottawa Gardens and Mahon Park. The Canadian Register of Historic Places describes a 105-metre-wide, 1.6-kilometre-long central garden boulevard, planned from 1906 by the North Vancouver Land and Improvement Company, with wide lots facing it.
Nearby areas: Central Lonsdale (west, across the City core), Moodyville (east, City), Lynn Valley (north-east, District, along Lynn Valley Road), and Upper Lonsdale (west, District side).

Transit: TransLink route 240 (Lynn Valley / Downtown) runs via Lynn Valley Road, Boulevard Crescent, Grand Boulevard East, 15th Street, Jones Avenue, Keith Road, Marine Drive and the Lions Gate Bridge to downtown Vancouver — the corridor has a direct downtown bus on its own street. Route 230 runs on Lonsdale Avenue west of the corridor to Lonsdale Quay and the SeaBus, which crosses to Waterfront Station in 12 minutes, every 15 minutes during the day.

Anchors beside the corridor: Queensbury Elementary (2020 Moody Avenue) and Ridgeway Elementary (420 East 8th Street) are the elementary schools beside the corridor, and Sutherland Secondary (1860 Sutherland Avenue) is the secondary school west of it; Lions Gate Hospital is at 231 East 15th Street, west of the corridor, and the North Vancouver City Library is at 120 West 14th Street.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect condo buyers in Boulevard

items.t: City side — plans and zoning (south of Highway 1): City of North Vancouver Official Community Plan Bylaw No. 8400 (2014, amended December 8, 2025) and Zoning Bylaw No. 6700. The Ground Oriented Zone, adopted December 8, 2025, allows up to 3 units on a lot of 280 m² or less, up to 4 units on a larger lot in the Low Rise Neighbourhood 1 designation, and up to 6 units in the Low Rise Neighbourhood 2 or Residential Level 4 designations; the adoption raised permitted units from 3 to 4 on nearly 4,300 properties. Grand Boulevard is also a City heritage character area — frontage and character rules, not just zoning, shape what can be built facing the boulevard.

District side — plans and zoning (north of Highway 1): District of North Vancouver Official Community Plan, Bylaw 7900, and Zoning Bylaw 3210. Section 525 (Bylaw 8799) sets R1 minimums of 4,000 m² / 30 m width / 34 m depth and R2 minimums of 660 m² / 18 m / 34 m, with modifiers R2(S1) 335 m² / 10 m, R2(S2) 1,100 m² / 24 m and R2(S3) 4,000 m² / 30 m; an R2 lot may hold a principal dwelling plus a secondary suite and a coach house, and since June 2024 three units total are permitted on single-family lots within the Urban Containment Boundary.

Hazard permits differ by side: on the City side the Streamside Protection Development Permit Area covers land within 15 metres of the top of bank of a watercourse or within 10 metres of the top of a ravine bank; on the District side OCP Bylaw 7900, Schedule B sets Development Permit Areas for Streamside Protection, Creek Hazard, Slope Hazard and Wildfire Hazard, any of which can apply on the District portion toward Lynn Valley.

Tax timing — both municipalities, different rates: City of North Vancouver 2026 taxes were due July 2, 2026; the 2026 total residential rate is 3.34028 per $1,000 of assessed value, plus a separate residential storm drainage rate of 0.10697 per $1,000. District of North Vancouver 2026 taxes were due July 2, 2026, with a 5% penalty after July 2, 2026 and a further 5% after September 1, 2026; the 2026 total residential rate is 3.28195 per $1,000, and single-family utility fees total $2,571.20 in 2026. Which bill a corridor address gets depends on which side of Highway 1 it sits.

One street name, two city halls. The same "Boulevard" address can be City (GO Zone, OCP Bylaw No. 8400, total tax rate 3.34028) or District (R1/R2 zones under Bylaw 3210, OCP Bylaw 7900, total rate 3.28195) depending on which side of Highway 1 it sits — never quote one side's density or tax numbers for the other.

The boulevard was a priced-to-exclude garden suburb. The historic-place record states the 1906 development required residences to cost more than $4,000 to construct so the area would maintain a high status, with owners signing a covenant binding heirs and successors — the heritage character area on today's City books descends from that scheme.

The park median is 105 metres wide and 1.6 kilometres long. That is the scale of the "boulevard" the houses face — a garden, not a traffic island — and it is part of the Green Necklace with Victoria Park, Ottawa Gardens and Mahon Park.

The City rewrote the corridor's density on December 8, 2025. The Ground Oriented Zone adopted that day raised permitted units from 3 to 4 on nearly 4,300 City properties and allows up to 6 units in the higher designations — a City-side side-street lot's value now turns on its OCP designation, while the District side still runs on principal + suite + coach house.

The elementary catchment may move for 2026/27. SD44's new Cloverley elementary school and its catchment review potentially impact the Queensbury and Ridgeway catchments — both schools sit beside this corridor — so a 2025 catchment statement for a corridor address should be re-run before a family writes.
There are no SnapStats numbers for this corridor.

blocks.text: TWO-MUNICIPALITY FLAG, stated at the top: "Boulevard" straddles the City/District line — the Grand Boulevard corridor is in the City of North Vancouver south of Highway 1 and continues in the District of North Vancouver as Grand Boulevard East to Boulevard Crescent and Lynn Valley Road.
Streets, schools and getting around Boulevard

items.t: South of Highway 1 the corridor (Grand Boulevard and Grand Boulevard Park, between Keith Road and Highway 1) is in the City of North Vancouver; north of the highway it continues in the District as Grand Boulevard East to Boulevard Crescent and Lynn Valley Road.

Where the housing stock is: predominantly freehold detached houses facing Grand Boulevard and on the side streets — the corridor's identity is its wide, park-like boulevard frontage. There is no townhouse concentration to name. Grand Boulevard Park is the corridor's central park, Grand Boulevard is a City heritage character area, and the boulevard forms part of the rectilinear system of boulevards and parks known as North Vancouver's Green Necklace, which also includes Victoria Park, Ottawa Gardens and Mahon Park.

Transit and roads: TransLink route 240 (Lynn Valley / Downtown) runs via Lynn Valley Road, Boulevard Crescent, Grand Boulevard East, 15th Street, Jones Avenue, Keith Road, Marine Drive and the Lions Gate Bridge to downtown Vancouver — the corridor has a direct downtown bus on its own street. Route 230 runs on Lonsdale Avenue west of the corridor, linking to Lonsdale Quay and the SeaBus (12 minutes to Waterfront Station, every 15 minutes during the day). Grand Boulevard is the main north–south road; Keith Road crosses the south end and Highway 1 crosses the north end of the City part.

Schools: School District 44 catchments are address-based; SD44 has elementary (K–7) and secondary (8–12) schools only, with no middle tier. Queensbury Elementary (K–7), 2020 Moody Avenue, and Ridgeway Elementary (K–7), 420 East 8th Street, are the elementary schools beside the corridor, and Sutherland Secondary (Grades 8–12), 1860 Sutherland Avenue, is the secondary school west of the corridor. SD44 is opening a new elementary school in the Cloverley neighbourhood for 2026/27, and its catchment review potentially impacts the Ridgeway, Brooksbank, Queensbury and Queen Mary catchments east of Lonsdale Avenue.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect townhome buyers in Boulevard

items.t: Why this section exists on a zero-stock corridor: there is no counted strata complex for the strata rules to attach to today. They are stated because (a) a buyer who widens the search to a strata townhouse in Central Lonsdale or Lynn Valley needs the diligence frame, and (b) the corridor house purchase that is this area's actual product is governed by the fee-simple and two-municipality rules that follow — which side of Highway 1 the lot sits on changes its minimums, taxes and permit areas entirely.

Form B diligence (any strata purchase off-corridor): Strata Property Act s. 59 — the Form B states the lot's monthly strata fees, amounts owing, approved special levies still payable, the CRF balance and an insurance summary, with the rules, current budget, any Rental Disclosure Statement and the most recent depreciation report attached; provided within 7 days, maximum $35 plus up to 25 cents per page. It does not apply to Chesterfield Manor (share purchase, excluded) or to a corridor house.

Depreciation reports / CRF minimum (any strata purchase off-corridor): since July 1, 2024, strata corporations with five or more lots must obtain a depreciation report every five years, not deferrable by vote; since Nov 1, 2023, at least 10% of the annual operating budget must go to the contingency reserve fund.

Rental-restriction bylaws are void / age bylaws: since Nov 24, 2022, no BC strata residential rental-restriction bylaw is valid (short-term rentals can still be restricted by bylaw), and only 55+ residency bylaws are lawful (Strata Property Act ss. 123.1/123.2 + Regulation 7.01, exemptions expanded May 1, 2023).

Fee-simple houses (the corridor's actual stock): Grand Boulevard is additionally a City heritage character area on the City side — frontage and character rules, not just zoning, shape what can be built facing the boulevard.

SSMUH as each municipality states it: City side — the GO Zone unit counts above (3 / 4 / 6 by lot size and designation) ARE the City's small-scale multi-unit framework for corridor lots; District side — principal dwelling plus secondary suite and coach house on an R2 lot, three units total on single-family lots within the Urban Containment Boundary since June 2024. There is no single "Boulevard SSMUH rule" — the municipality decides.

Hazards — City side: the City's Streamside Protection Development Permit Area covers land within 15 metres of the top of bank of a watercourse or within 10 metres of the top of a ravine bank, and a development permit is required before new development there.

Hazards — District side: District OCP Bylaw 7900, Schedule B sets Development Permit Areas for Streamside Protection, Creek Hazard, Slope Hazard and Wildfire Hazard, any of which can apply on the District portion toward Lynn Valley.

Tax timing — both municipalities, different rates: City side — 2026 taxes were due July 2, 2026; the 2026 residential municipal-general rate is 1.89202 and the total residential rate is 3.34028 per $1,000 of assessed value, plus a separate residential storm drainage rate of 0.10697 per $1,000. District side — 2026 taxes were due July 2, 2026, with a 5% penalty after July 2, 2026 and a further 5% after September 1, 2026; the 2026 residential municipal rate is 1.83419 and the total residential rate is 3.28195 per $1,000, and single-family utility fees total $2,571.20 in 2026. Confirm the municipality on title before comparing either figure.
One street name, two city halls.

The boulevard was a priced-to-exclude garden suburb. The Canadian Register of Historic Places records Grand Boulevard as North Vancouver's most prominent garden subdivision, planned from 1906 by the North Vancouver Land and Improvement Company, with early building restrictions including a provision that residences must cost more than $4,000 to construct to keep the area prestigious — the wide lots facing the median are the surviving form of that scheme.

The park median is 105 metres wide and 1.6 kilometres long. The Register describes the central garden boulevard between the two sides of the roadway at that scale, facing mansions and bungalows with views of Burrard Inlet, the mountains and downtown Vancouver — the frontage a corridor buyer is actually paying for.
The City rewrote the corridor's density on December 8, 2025.

The two municipalities are different sizes entirely. The City's 2021 Census population was 58,120 on 11.83 km²; the District's was 88,168 (Statistics Canada, 2021 Census, via the City census backgrounder and the Focus on Geography Series) — the compact city core and the sprawling district meet on this one corridor.

Care and library anchors sit west of the corridor, not on it. Lions Gate Hospital, 231 East 15th Street (Vancouver Coastal Health), and the North Vancouver Urgent and Primary Care Centre, 221 West Esplanade, serve the area from the west side; the North Vancouver City Library is at 120 West 14th Street.
There are no SnapStats numbers for this corridor — by design, not omission.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Boulevard

items.t: Two rulebooks, one corridor — read the side that matches the title: City side — City of North Vancouver Official Community Plan Bylaw No. 8400 (2014, amended December 8, 2025) and Zoning Bylaw No. 6700. District side — District of North Vancouver Official Community Plan, Bylaw 7900, and Zoning Bylaw 3210. Neither municipality's bylaws apply on the other side of Highway 1.

City side — GO Zone density (adopted December 8, 2025): a lot of 280 m² or less allows up to 3 units; a lot over 280 m² allows up to 4 units in the Low Rise Neighbourhood 1 designation and up to 6 units in the Low Rise Neighbourhood 2 or Residential Level 4 designations; the GO Zone adoption raised permitted units from 3 to 4 on nearly 4,300 properties. Subdivision minimum widths are in.

District side — added units: an R2 lot may hold a principal dwelling plus a secondary suite and a coach house, and since June 2024 three units total are permitted on single-family lots within the Urban Containment Boundary; the District GeoWeb SSMUH classification (potentially up to 6 units above 280 m² within 400 m of a frequent-transit stop) is parcel-specific. Never quote one side's density numbers for the other.

Heritage / covenant diligence (City side): Grand Boulevard is a City heritage character area in the Green Necklace system — a boulevard-facing rebuild carries character expectations a side-street lot does not; check the title and the City's heritage record for the specific lot before pricing a teardown.

Bare-land strata rules (the 1555 Grand Boulevard form — the BC strata block applies in full IF title confirms strata tenure): Form B diligence (fees, amounts owed, levies, CRF balance, insurance summary; provided within 7 days, max $35 + 25¢/page); depreciation reports on a 5-year cycle for stratas with 5+ lots since July 1, 2024 (a single-lot form sits outside that 5+ threshold on its face — confirm the plan's lot count on title); minimum 10% CRF contribution since November 1, 2023; rental-restriction bylaws void since November 24, 2022 (short-term restrictions may still apply by bylaw); only 55+ age bylaws valid under Strata Property Act ss. 123.1/123.2, with May 1, 2023 exemptions (younger spouse/partner, caregivers, legacy residents, defined children); a listing's "45+" line is not a valid BC age bylaw.

ALR rules (for completeness — no corridor ALR parcel is confirmed here): subdivision within the ALR requires ALC approval; ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s. 6; Strata Property Act s. 239; Agricultural Land Commission Act s. 21(1)); ALC residence caps: principal ≤500 m², suite within the principal residence only, additional residence 90 m² (≤40 ha) / 186 m² (>40 ha). Farm class is three-tiered ($2,500 on 0.8–4 ha; $2,500 + 5% of the land's value over 4 ha; $10,000 under 0.8 ha; applications by October 31) — a flat "$2,500+" line is an error.

Property taxes — stated per side: City side — 2026 taxes due July 2, 2026; the 2026 residential municipal-general rate is 1.89202 and the total residential rate is 3.34028 per $1,000 of assessed value, plus a separate residential storm drainage rate of 0.10697 per $1,000. District side — 2026 taxes due July 2, 2026, with a 5% penalty after July 2, 2026 and a further 5% after September 1, 2026; the 2026 residential municipal rate is 1.83419 and the total residential rate is 3.28195 per $1,000, and single-family utility fees total $2,571.20 in 2026.

The boulevard was a priced-to-exclude garden suburb (1906, City heritage record): the historic-place record states the 1906 development required residences to cost more than $4,000 to construct so the area would maintain a high status, with owners signing a covenant binding heirs and successors — the heritage character area on today's City books descends from that scheme.

The park median is the scale of a garden, not a traffic island: 105 metres wide and 1.6 kilometres long, part of the Green Necklace with Victoria Park, Ottawa Gardens and Mahon Park — boulevard-facing lots front a park, which is the frontage premium and the character constraint in one fact.

The City rewrote its side's density on December 8, 2025: the Ground Oriented Zone adopted that day raised permitted units from 3 to 4 on nearly 4,300 City properties and allows up to 6 units in the higher designations — a City-side side-street lot's value now turns on its OCP designation, while the District side still runs on principal + suite + coach house.

The elementary catchment may move for 2026/27: SD44's new Cloverley elementary school and its catchment review potentially impact the Queensbury and Ridgeway catchments — both schools sit beside this corridor — so a 2025 catchment statement for a corridor address should be re-run before a family writes.
